title: Start Simple, Grow Complex
equation: Survival Odds = Simplicity at Launch ÷ Complexity at Launch
hook: The version you're planning to launch is probably three versions too big.
statement: Every complex system that works started as a simple system that worked.
explainer: You can't design something complicated from scratch and expect it to run. Complexity that works gets grown, not installed. So launch small, make it work, then add.
sop: Write the smallest version that works end to end for one real customer.
Score Simplicity at Launch and Complexity at Launch from 1 to 10.
Divide them. Below 1, cut features until the core stands alone.
Ship that, then add only what real usage asks for.
equation_example: Simplicity at Launch 8, Complexity at Launch 2. 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Well above 1, so it's simple enough to work and then grow. Below 1 means it's too tangled and likely to fall apart before it ever settles.
question: Write down the smallest version of your next launch that would still work for one customer.
closing_statement: Make it work small. Let it earn every extra layer.
caption:
Principle Nº 334: Start Simple, Grow Complex

The version you're planning to launch is probably three versions too big.

Every complex system that works started as a simple system that worked.

Your turn: Write down the smallest version of your next launch that would still work for one customer.
